problem: It says classic nodes treat FDF as an error 'and do not disturb the bus'. A classic controller that sees the recessive FDF (and res) bit where it expects dominant raises a form error and transmits an error frame, which destroys the FD frame. The claim also contradicts the later line in the same section that a classic controller on the same bus rejects FD frames.
fix: FDF (FD Format) marks an FD frame. A classic controller sees a recessive bit where it expects dominant, raises a form error and sends an error frame, so the FD frame is destroyed. Classic and FD nodes therefore cannot share one bus; every controller and transceiver on the segment must support CAN FD.

where: Figure (frame field array) and its aria text
problem: The aria says the identifier and bit-rate switch fields are highlighted, but the classic row marks 'ID' plus 'DATA' (as 'live'), and the CAN FD row marks only 'BRS'. The FD identifier is not highlighted, and the 'live' mark on classic DATA has no meaning given in the caption.
fix: Mark the identifier cell in both rows, and mark BRS in the CAN FD row only; drop the 'live' mark on DATA or explain it in the caption.

problem: The classic row shows IDE (and RTR) between the identifier and DLC, but the FD row jumps from ID straight to FDF, so a student may think an FD frame has no IDE bit or that FDF replaces the whole control field.
fix: Show the FD control field as ID, FDF, res, BRS, ESI, DLC (IDE still present), or note in the caption that only the new and changed bits are drawn.
